This reduced genetic diversity could further jeopardize future population health and genetic variability.

On January 9, 2015, French security forces ended a three-day siege involving two brothers, Said and Cherif Kouachi, who had attacked the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo and were later cornered at a printing facility in Dammartin-en-Goele. An employee named Lilian Lepere provided critical intelligence to police via text messages from inside the building, helping them plan the assault that killed both brothers.

Meanwhile, Amedy Coulibaly, suspected of being an accomplice, took hostages at a kosher supermarket in Paris. He was also killed during a raid after threatening more violence if authorities attacked the Kouachi brothers. The attacks resulted in 20 deaths and raised concerns about the threat posed by returning foreign fighters to Western countries.

The Kouachis were known to authorities due to prior convictions related to terrorism, including ties to al-Qaeda in Yemen. Their actions were linked to Al-Qaida's branch in Yemen, which claimed responsibility for the attack.

Jahi McMath, declared brain dead in 2014 after a routine surgery at Children's Hospital Oakland, remains supported by her family who continues to fight for her right to life. Her mother, Nailah Winkfield, has released public updates stating that Jahi is "as healthy and beautiful as ever," challenging medical opinions. The family moved Jahi from California to New Jersey in 2014 due to a religious exemption allowing continued life support despite brain death diagnosis. They have also filed lawsuits against the hospital over the surgery and organ donation claims. Medical experts argue that being brain dead means essentially being dead, but Jahi's case continues to draw attention and support from those who believe she is still alive.

The $50 toys were highly sought after during the holiday season, with some selling for up to $350 on third-party sites due to scarcity. Parents and children reported frustration when the toys did not hatch despite following instructions, leading to complaints and calls to customer service. Spin Master acknowledged receiving numerous complaints but stated they provided troubleshooting support and replacements where necessary. The lawsuit alleges deceptive business practices and seeks damages for consumer law violations, unfair competition, false advertising, breach of warranty, and unjust enrichment.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) has confirmed that 32 out of 33 tested dolphins have shown signs of this virus, with 11 cases genetically confirmed. Since July 1, over 330 dolphin strandings have been reported from New York to North Carolina, with the majority occurring in Virginia.

This event is reminiscent of a similar morbillivirus outbreak in 1987-88, which resulted in nearly 800 deaths. Scientists believe that the virus has re-emerged due to dolphins losing their immunity over time. While there's no vaccine available for wild dolphin populations, researchers are monitoring the situation and expect the die-off to continue until spring 2014 as the virus spreads southward with migrating dolphins.

John Doe No. 89, now named Andy Drath, has been identified after being missing for over three decades. Andy was a 16-year-old boy from Chicago when he went missing in late 1978 or early 1979 and was found dead in San Francisco with multiple gunshot wounds. His case remained cold until Gacy investigators used new DNA technology to match his tissue samples to his half-sister, Willia Wertheimer. This breakthrough led to the identification of Andy Drath as one of John Wayne Gacy's victims. The Cook County Sheriff's Office credits this case as illustrating that "never give up" on cold cases and has closed 12 such cases related to Gacy since 2011, with five people found alive and reunited with their families.

Charlo Greene, a former TV reporter who quit live on air to advocate for marijuana legalization and opened the Alaska Cannabis Club, faces up to 54 years in prison due to charges of "misconduct involving a controlled substance." Her case highlights issues with the ongoing war on drugs and raises concerns about racial disparities in drug enforcement. Despite her activism, Greene struggles for support as few people have rallied behind her legal troubles. The charges stem from Greene's club operating before retail regulations were established, but critics argue she should face lesser penalties like fines. This case could have broader implications as more states move towards cannabis legalization.

Other notable items include John Lennon’s piano and drawings, and Jim Morrison’s lyrics. Elvis Presley's sweat-stained suit from his Las Vegas performances is also up for auction, potentially selling for $100,000 to $200,000.

A California man captured a rare incident on video where a great white shark breached a shark cage off Guadalupe Island, Mexico. The diver inside, Ming Chan, emerged shaken but unharmed after the shark broke through the cage while attempting to bite bait. The videographer explained that the shark was temporarily blinded and unable to swim backward when it hit the cage, causing it to break. Despite the frightening experience, both the diver and the videographer plan to return for future shark encounters. The incident highlights the temporary nature of a shark's aggressive behavior during feeding and emphasizes the safety measures in place by the tour operators.

Dixon posted a viral photo on Facebook depicting the meat as rodent-shaped with what appeared to be a tail. After Dixon's attorney sent the product for DNA testing, results confirmed it was indeed chicken. KFC conducted an internal investigation and stated that Dixon's claim was false, requesting him to apologize and cease making false claims. The company emphasized that the product was chicken and not a rat as Dixon alleged.

The Rabbit Who Wants to Fall Asleep, a self-published children's book by Swedish psychologist Carl-Johan Forssen Ehrlin, has become a bestseller on Amazon. The 26-page story uses psychological techniques and language patterns to help children fall asleep more easily. Parents are advised to read the book slowly and yawn during the narrative, which they believe transfers to their child's behavior. The book features characters like Uncle Yawn and Sleepy Snail who guide Roger the Rabbit through relaxation exercises. Positive feedback from parents highlights its effectiveness in helping children sleep faster. Ehrlin claims his method is a form of verbal hypnosis designed to induce relaxation and solve sleep-related problems. The book has been translated into seven languages and outsells other popular titles on Amazon.

Archaeologists have discovered an escape tunnel at the site of Sobibor, a Nazi death camp in German-occupied Poland during World War II. The 32-foot-long tunnel, found five feet below the surface and stretching beyond the barbed-wire fences, provides physical evidence that prisoners attempted to dig their way out. The sonderkommando, prisoners tasked with managing the gas chambers, likely constructed this escape route.

While the tunnel's discoverers believe it was intended for escape, there is no evidence suggesting anyone successfully used it before a major uprising in October 1943, when about 600 prisoners managed to break out. The tunnel was probably discovered and its creators executed; subsequent excavations were likely filled in by Nazi officials after the revolt.

John Forbes Nash Jr., a renowned mathematician whose life was depicted in the Oscar-winning film "A Beautiful Mind," was recommended for Princeton University's graduate program by Richard J. Duffin with the succinct statement: "He is a mathematical genius." Nash was accepted into Princeton, where he later won his PhD and developed the concept of the "Nash equilibrium" in his dissertation titled "Non-cooperative games." This work significantly impacted game theory and earned him the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences in 1994. Nash passed away in a car accident with his wife Alicia on May 23, 2015, shortly after receiving the Abel Prize for mathematics. Princeton University has made available documents from Nash's academic record, including Duffin's recommendation letter and his dissertation.

In 2011, Robert McCoy was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death in Louisiana for a triple homicide committed in 2008. His defense attorney, Larry English, conceded guilt during the trial despite McCoy's objections, aiming to secure a lesser sentence. This strategy was upheld by the Louisiana Supreme Court, but McCoy now argues that his Sixth Amendment rights were violated.

English believed the case against McCoy was too strong and focused on seeking mercy rather than acquittal. McCoy maintained his innocence throughout, claiming he was framed by local police. The U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear McCoy's appeal, which questions whether a defense attorney can concede guilt over their client’s objections without violating constitutional rights.

The case highlights the tension between a defendant's autonomy and an attorney's strategic decision-making in high-stakes cases like capital murder trials. While some argue that such concessions are necessary to avoid harsher penalties, others contend they undermine the accused's right to control their defense.

The Dutch Safety Board released its final report on the July 2014 downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 over eastern Ukraine, concluding that a Russian-made Buk missile caused the crash, killing all 298 people aboard. The report does not identify who fired the missile but suggests it was likely from an area controlled by pro-Russian separatists. Paint matching and other evidence support this conclusion. However, Russia disputes these findings, claiming the Ukrainian army could have been responsible with older missile models. The report also states that Ukraine should have closed its airspace in the conflict zone on the day of the crash. While it does not assign blame, the Dutch government is urging Russia to cooperate in the ongoing criminal investigation.

The George Washington Bridge witnessed a significant increase in suicide attempts and completions in 2012, with 18 people jumping to their deaths—the highest number on record. This was accompanied by an all-time high of 43 attempted suicides. The bridge has long been known as a frequent site for such incidents, typically surpassing the combined totals from other local bridges.

In response to these events, Port Authority police intensified patrols and considered updating surveillance systems. Notably, in May 2013, Officer Jesse Turano made a heroic rescue of a man attempting suicide by grabbing him mid-air as he tried to jump off the bridge. This was part of Turano's efforts that year, where he is reported to have saved at least four other individuals from jumping.

The incidents are linked to economic hardships and mental health issues, with one rescued individual citing unemployment as his primary reason for attempting suicide. Officer Turano's actions highlight the ongoing challenges in preventing such tragedies on the bridge.

Franklin released a statement clarifying that no fight occurred and that she and LaBelle are still friends. The lawsuit aims to ensure that her truth is widely known.

Fleming, a 59-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis who is confined to a wheelchair, plans to appeal the decision. She argued her condition would lead to an undignified and painful death, but the court deemed it impossible to tailor legislation for individual cases without harming public interest. In 2013, Med Express sued Amy Nicholls and Dennis Rogan for giving negative feedback on eBay. Nicholls had complained about extra postage charges after purchasing a microscope light. Despite Med Express's apology and withdrawal of the lawsuit, Nicholls and her legal team (Jeffrey Nye and Thomas Haren) filed counterclaims alleging frivolous conduct and malice.

The case went to trial in 2014, with Judge James Leaver ruling that Med Express and its founder Richard Radey must pay $19,250 in attorney fees. The judge found that the lawsuit was baseless as Nicholls' feedback contained both opinion and factual statements, which were true. Radey had a history of similar lawsuits against out-of-state customers.

The ruling is seen as a victory for consumer rights, demonstrating that companies cannot use legal action to silence negative feedback. Public Citizen's Paul Levy praised the decision, emphasizing its importance for protecting free speech online.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the sudden discontinuation of 500 and 1000 rupee notes, effective midnight local time, to combat corruption and black money. This move, part of a broader crackdown on illegal cash holdings, represents about 85% of India's circulating currency. New 2000 rupee notes will be introduced over the next three to four weeks. The decision has caused widespread disruption, with long queues at ATMs as people try to withdraw smaller denominations and banks closing for two days. While some praised it as a bold anti-corruption measure, others expressed concerns about its impact on small businesses and the informal economy during the transition period.

Researchers suggest land use changes could help reduce the zone's size.

Orpinas argues against the common belief that relational aggression is primarily a female behavior, citing other studies and authors like Rosalind Wiseman who have challenged this notion. Wiseman emphasizes the need for more attention on boys' social challenges and suggests that both genders face similar social issues. She advocates for changing cultural expectations of boys to foster better emotional lives and social competence.

The U.S. federal government shutdown has significantly impacted various agencies and programs responsible for science, health, and public services. Key points include:

- **Food and Drug Administration (FDA):** Food safety inspections and research activities are suspended, though some emergency functions continue.

- **Small Business Administration (SBA):** New loan guarantees are suspended, affecting small businesses seeking financial support.

A study by the CDC estimates that a fetus infected with Zika during the first trimester has a 1% to 14% risk of developing microcephaly, a condition where the head is much smaller than expected due to incomplete brain development. This range accounts for varying levels of Zika transmission in different scenarios. The research, based on data from Brazil and French Polynesia, highlights that risks are highest early in pregnancy but still exist later. Other birth defects linked to Zika include eye problems such as retinal lesions and hemorrhaging, which could lead to severe visual impairment.

The study underscores the substantial risk posed by Zika during pregnancy, particularly for women living in areas where the virus is prevalent or likely to spread. Health systems need to prepare for an increase in cases of microcephaly and other birth defects, potentially overwhelming resources in developing countries. Further research is needed to understand if other factors, such as environmental conditions or previous infections, might influence the risk of Zika-related birth defects.

While some critics view the new oath as ineffective or symbolic, supporters argue it serves as a reminder to uphold professional standards and could potentially influence behavior. She was hospitalized after suffering a stroke earlier that week. The couple met when Stan was supposed to take Joan's friend on a blind date but ended up taking Joan instead. They had two children: J.C., born in 1950, and Jan, who died shortly after birth.

A study led by academics from the Universities of Nottingham and Bristol has uncovered how animals link changes in seasons to their fertility. The research reveals that melatonin, produced during long winter nights in the pineal gland, controls the production of two different types of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) within a specific region of the pituitary gland. In winter, VEGF blocks blood vessel growth, while in summer it promotes growth between regions of the pituitary, allowing VEGF to act as a messenger controlling sex hormone-producing cells and fertility.

This discovery provides insight into how day length affects seasonal changes in animals, including sheep, which could help farmers manage breeding seasons. The findings also have broader implications for understanding human biology, particularly in relation to hormonal diseases and seasonal immune function.

The shark is estimated to have been between 18-20 feet long. Authorities closed nearby beaches for safety reasons. This incident marks a rare fatal shark attack in California; the last one occurred in 2008.

This issue has affected major hubs including Miami, Dallas-Fort Worth, Chicago's O'Hare, and New York's LaGuardia Airport. To address the problem, American Airlines is offering 150% pay for pilots to work these dates, but the union argues this violates their contract. Professional poker player Jacob Brundage lost $7,000 in cash and chips after leaving his black tote bag in an Uber minivan while traveling to the Rio for the World Series of Poker. Realizing his mistake around 9 p.m., he tried contacting the driver through the app but was unsuccessful due to a dead phone battery. Fortunately, Brundage encountered Uber employees at the casino who helped locate and retrieve the lost item within an hour. The driver returned the bag, and Brundage rewarded him with $200 plus another $100 for assistance from the Uber team. This incident is reportedly the most valuable item ever left in an Uber car in Las Vegas, highlighting both a lapse in Brundage's attention and the honesty of the Uber driver.

The shutdown also affected services such as passport processing, food inspections, and federal loan programs.

Vint Cerf, often referred to as the "father of the Internet," warned at the American Association for the Advancement of Science meeting in San Jose that future archaeologists might struggle to interpret 21st-century civilization due to potential loss of digital records. He emphasized the need to preserve all necessary data for correct interpretation and suggested that current reliance on digital storage could lead to an "information black hole." Cerf cited examples such as Doris Kearns Goodwin's work, which heavily relied on physical documents, suggesting future historians might face difficulties if similar records are lost or uninterpretable. To address this issue, he proposed the concept of "digital vellum," involving creating a digital snapshot at the time an item is stored to ensure its reproducibility in the future. Cerf also highlighted the importance of maintaining physical copies for critical documents and photographs.

The attorneys involved argue that minimum wage should have been significantly higher, emphasizing the need for fair compensation for restaurant workers in light of current economic conditions.

These males often copulate with immature female spiders who have not yet developed external reproductive organs and are thus unable to consume their mates. The males use their fangs to cut through the immature females' exoskeletons and deposit sperm into their internal reproductive structures, called spermatheca. Once the females mature, they can produce offspring from these matings.

This behavior is significant because it allows male widow spiders to mate with multiple partners without risking cannibalism, which is typical for mature female widows. Tamerlan Tsarnaev's body, who died after the Boston Marathon bombing and subsequent manhunt, remains unburied as his family seeks an independent autopsy and a burial site in Massachusetts. His death certificate lists causes of death as gunshot wounds and blunt trauma. The funeral home holding his remains is facing resistance from cemeteries due to public backlash; however, the owner believes everyone deserves a proper burial. Meanwhile, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, his younger brother, is being held and treated for injuries sustained during the manhunt. Intelligence agencies are under scrutiny regarding their handling of Tamerlan Tsarnaev before the attacks. The brothers were initially planning to attack the Boston July 4th celebration but changed plans due to timing issues. Three friends of Dzhokhar Tsarnaev have been charged with covering up evidence, and an independent review is being conducted into potential intelligence failures.

Thousands of Occupy Oakland protesters participated in a general strike on November 2, 2011, closing streets, squares, banks, and the port. The protest began at Frank H Ogawa Plaza, where thousands marched to various locations including banks, the port, and other financial institutions. Protesters aimed to highlight economic inequality and demand change from the 1%.

Key events included:
- A march on the Port of Oakland led to its closure by protesters.
- Vandalism occurred at several businesses, though no arrests were made as of late Wednesday.
- The city maintained a minimal police presence but was prepared for potential issues.

The protest was largely peaceful, with some minor incidents. Mayor Jean Quan and City Administrator Deanna Santana emphasized the need for safety and peaceful demonstrations. Overall, the strike demonstrated solidarity among protesters and highlighted their message to the public.

A man named Michael David Elliot, who is serving five life sentences for four 1993 murders, escaped from the Ionia Correctional Facility in Michigan around 7 p.m. Sunday. He managed to break out through the sally port and flee using a hole in the fencing system. After escaping, he carjacked a woman with a box cutter and drove approximately 100 miles to Elkhart, Indiana.

Elliot was arrested early Monday evening in Kankakee Township, LaPorte County, Indiana, after stealing four vehicles during his 24-hour escape. He was found in a snowbank where he had lost control of the stolen vehicle. Elliot is being held without bond on felony car theft and resisting charges.

In the Democratic race, Bernie Sanders triumphed over Hillary Clinton with a significant margin, signaling his candidacy as a serious threat for the nomination. Clinton acknowledged her loss but emphasized her resilience and vowed to continue fighting for change in every state. The results highlight generational and gender tensions among supporters, with both candidates facing criticism and defending their platforms. Donald Trump's victory party was marked by boasting about winning and making populist promises, while ignoring Clinton's performance.

President Trump criticized two women who accused Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh of sexual misconduct, calling their allegations a "con game" and dismissing one as drunk and with memory gaps. The Republican-controlled Senate Judiciary Committee is set to hold a hearing on Thursday for Kavanaugh and his accuser Christine Blasey Ford. Despite the accusations, Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell remains confident in Kavanaugh's confirmation. Democrats have called for an FBI investigation but face opposition from Republicans who argue that the process should be fair and non-partisan. The situation has intensified political tensions ahead of the hearing and upcoming votes on Kavanaugh's nomination.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) released a preliminary report detailing the final moments of the flight.

Jimmy Kimmel criticized Senator Bill Cassidy's health care bill on his late-night show, arguing it would not protect people with pre-existing conditions as promised. Health care analysts generally agree with Kimmel’s assessment that the bill could lead to significant cuts in Medicaid and potentially millions losing coverage. Cassidy countered that the bill would still provide adequate coverage for those with pre-existing conditions. President Trump supported the bill but also emphasized protections for such individuals. The debate highlights the complexity of health policy, with Kimmel using his platform to advocate based on personal experience, while Cassidy defended the bill's provisions.

Brendt Christensen, a 28-year-old former University of Illinois graduate student, faces new charges of kidnapping resulting in death for Yingying Zhang, a visiting scholar from China who disappeared in June. The federal grand jury indicted Christensen on additional counts of making false statements to FBI agents and found that the crime was "especially heinous, cruel or depraved," involving torture or serious physical abuse after substantial planning and premeditation. If convicted, Christensen could face the death penalty or life imprisonment without parole. Surveillance footage and audio recordings allegedly show Christensen's involvement in Zhang’s disappearance. Christensen initially claimed to have been playing video games all day on June 9 but later admitted to picking up an Asian woman who was waiting for a bus. He is tentatively set to go to trial on February 27, with his lawyer stating no comment at this time.

This shift came after new information emerged during investigations into the incident, which killed four Americans including Ambassador Christopher Stevens.

The Obama administration's accounts of the attack have been criticized for their inconsistency; early statements suggested it was a response to an anti-Islamic video, while later assessments labeled it a terrorist act. The White House maintains that its evolving narrative reflected new intelligence findings rather than attempts to downplay the severity of the event.

Republican critics argue that the administration knew the attack was premeditated but failed to disclose this information to avoid highlighting security failures. Democrats, including Senator John Kerry, have called for more transparency and details about security measures at U.S. embassies abroad.

Manganiello proposed to Vergara during their Christmas vacation in Hawaii. The couple has been enjoying a whirlwind romance since going public in June and celebrated Manganiello's 38th birthday together. They were introduced at the White House Correspondents Dinner in May.

Vergara, 42, was seen wearing a large diamond ring shortly after the proposal. She expressed her happiness on social media, calling Manganiello her "love" and "best friend." Manganiello previously described Vergara as his "dream girl," praising her beauty and personality.

U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer sent an open letter to San Diego Mayor Bob Filner, urging him to resign due to sexual harassment allegations from 14 women. Boxer emphasized the severity of these accusations, particularly those involving victims of sexual assault. Filner had been undergoing intensive behavioral therapy for two weeks but completed it earlier than planned and will continue as an outpatient.

City Council members Marti Emerald and Myrtle Cole called for Filner's resignation, making it unanimous among all nine council members. They cited new allegations from female staffers who reported daily harassment and abuse. Additionally, the city attorney changed locks at Filner’s office to protect potential evidence during his absence.

Filner is facing a sexual harassment lawsuit filed by former communications director Irene McCormack Jackson, with other women also coming forward with similar accusations. His legal team stated he would continue therapy as an outpatient after completing his intensive program early.

Skye McCole Bartusiak, who played Mel Gibson's daughter in the 2000 film "The Patriot," passed away at age 21 on Saturday in her Texas home. The cause of death is unknown but her mother suggests it may have been related to a seizure that led to choking. Bartusiak had a successful acting career as a child, appearing in films like "The Cider House Rules" and "Don't Say a Word," as well as TV shows such as "24," "Lost," and "House M.D." She was also preparing to produce and direct her first feature film. Known for her kind nature, Bartusiak had suffered from epileptic seizures since infancy, with them resurfacing in recent days before her death.

Adventurer Johnny Strange, who gained fame for climbing the seven summits by age 17, died at 23 after crashing during wingsuit BASE jumping in the Swiss Alps. The crash occurred on a day with reported strong winds. Strange had recently spoken about his trip to Switzerland and posted videos of his jumps, including one filmed just days before his death. Model Gigi Hadid remembered him as having an adventurous spirit.

Strange was known for taking risks and performing dangerous stunts like wingsuit BASE jumping, which involves leaping from heights while wearing a wingsuit that extends flight time and range. The inherent dangers were highlighted by the deaths of other jumpers, including fellow adventurer Dean Potter. Strange acknowledged these risks but continued to pursue such activities.

Donald Trump is set to moderate a presidential debate hosted by Newsmax and aired on Ion Television on December 27 in Iowa. This event highlights Trump's significant influence among conservative voters, particularly the Tea Party wing, who may not agree with him but see him as an outsider to Washington and media establishments. The debate will be open-ended rather than topic-specific, covering a wide range of issues. Newsmax Media's Christopher Ruddy emphasizes that their readers support Trump for his anti-establishment stance. This debate marks another memorable moment in an already spectacle-filled primary season and underscores how reality TV elements are increasingly intertwined with political processes.

The meeting between the two leaders remains uncertain, as Peña Nieto’s team evaluates the situation.

Peña Nieto's decision has faced criticism from some in Mexico who believe he should cancel or postpone the visit. Lady Gaga's "Born This Way" debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart with 1,108,000 copies sold in its first week, marking the highest sales week since 2005 and only the 17th album to achieve this feat since SoundScan began tracking data in 1991. The album also set a new record for the largest digital sales week with 662,000 downloads, accounting for 60% of its first-week total. Amazon's controversial one-day sale of the album for 99 cents significantly contributed to these impressive numbers by selling an estimated 440,000 copies. This success makes Lady Gaga the fifth woman and only the second pop artist in SoundScan history to achieve a million-plus sales week.

Ross William Ulbricht, known online as "Dread Pirate Roberts," has been arrested for allegedly running the underground drug marketplace Silk Road from a San Francisco library. The FBI seized the site in 2013 and charged Ulbricht with numerous crimes including narcotics trafficking, money laundering, and attempted murder. Over two years, Silk Road generated $1.2 billion in sales and $80 million in commissions for Ulbricht. He used Tor to conceal his identity and Bitcoin for transactions. The indictment alleges that Ulbricht paid for a murder-for-hire attempt against a user threatening to expose Silk Road users. Authorities identified him through online activity, including forum posts promoting the site under the name "Altoid." Ulbricht's background includes studying physics and engineering before moving to San Francisco. He was arrested at the Glen Park Branch Library in San Francisco.

A study from Stanford University researchers analyzed body camera footage of 981 traffic stops by Oakland Police Department officers in 2014, revealing that police officers spoke more respectfully to white drivers than black drivers. Key findings include:

- Officers used respectful terms like "ma'am" and "sir" more often with white drivers.
- White drivers were more likely to hear polite phrases ("please", "thank you") compared to black drivers.
- Black drivers were called by their first names or informal titles more frequently.

The study controlled for officer race, severity of infraction, stop location, and outcome. It found that white community members were 57% more likely to hear respectful utterances than black community members. The research demonstrates the potential of body camera footage as a data source for studying police-community interactions.

Lead researcher Jennifer Eberhardt emphasized that these findings do not equate to racial bias but highlight disparities in how officers communicate with different communities. The study aims to inform police training

Congressman Daniel Sickles shot Philip Barton Key, son of the author of "The Star-Spangled Banner," in 1859 after discovering his wife's affair. The trial became a sensation as Sickles successfully pleaded temporary insanity to avoid first-degree murder charges. Public opinion largely supported him, viewing the act as justifiable revenge for adultery. Despite initial support, public sentiment eventually turned against Sickles due to his ongoing affairs and other scandals. His legal defense of "temporary insanity" influenced future cases but was later restricted by legislation. Throughout his life, Sickles faced controversy and scandal, including a failed divorce from his wife Teresa and a brief affair with the former Queen of Spain. Despite these challenges, he remained politically active until his death at 93.

The National Liberation Front of Corsica (FLNC), a militant group seeking independence for Corsica from France since 1976, has announced it will lay down its arms and pursue political goals instead. This decision comes after nearly four decades of armed struggle and marks the end of an era of terrorism on the island, which includes bombings, robberies, and assaults.

The FLNC stated that they have initiated a demilitarization process without preconditions and emphasized their commitment to conventional political channels for achieving independence. The group cited recent legislative successes, such as a law limiting property purchases by non-residents, as part of the rationale behind this decision.

This move towards peaceful means follows similar actions taken by other separatist groups, like ETA in Spain, which has also decommissioned some weapons and moved towards political dialogue. Two twin sisters from Australia, both 29 years old, died after a suicide pact at a gun range near Denver, Colorado. One sister died while the other survived and is now in stable condition. The incident occurred at the Family Shooting Center within Cherry Creek State Park. According to investigators, physical evidence, surveillance footage, and the surviving sister's statement all support that this was indeed a suicide attempt. The women had been firing guns for nearly 90 minutes before turning the weapons on themselves.

The surviving twin would not disclose her reasons during an interview with police. Family members were shocked by the incident; they had traveled to the U.S. and Canada regularly but had not shared their plans or feelings about returning home. The sisters, named Candace and Kristin Hermeler, received degrees from Australian universities and had been traveling extensively since graduation.

Adele's latest album, 21, is a breakup album focused on her heartbreak from a former lover. The songs are deeply personal and emotional, inspired by drunken diary entries. Adele describes the album as "cheap therapy" for herself but hopes it will offer comfort to fans experiencing similar heartaches. Her raw vocals and candid lyrics make the album stand out. Additionally, Adele expresses interest in exploring American musical traditions like country and bluegrass for future projects.

Kim Cattrall, 61, has revealed her strained relationships with her "Sex and the City" co-stars during an interview with Piers Morgan for ITV. She stated that she never considered herself a friend to Sarah Jessica Parker, Kristin Davis, or Cynthia Nixon, but rather a colleague. The actress denied rumors that her demands led to the cancellation of the third film, calling them "ridiculous." Cattrall claimed she only said no to the project for nearly a year and has always prioritized her role over personal relationships.

Cattrall also discussed her decision not to have children due to the demanding schedule of filming "Sex and the City," which began shortly after her marriage in 1998. She expressed regret that her co-stars did not reach out more often, describing their relationship as "toxic." Despite this, she has since mentored young actresses.

LulzSec, a notorious hacker group known for its high-profile cyber attacks and public disclosures, has announced it will be retiring after 50 days of hacking activities. The group released a data dump containing information from several targets, including AOL, AT&T, Battlefield Heroes, FBI, Hackforums.net, NATO-bookshop.org, US Navy, corporate office networks, private investigators, gaming forums, and routers.

LulzSec's final statement emphasizes its desire to inspire change through their actions, despite facing significant backlash. They also express support for the AntiSec movement, which aims to expose government-classified information.

Sen. Rand Paul is seeking legislation in Kentucky that would allow him to simultaneously run for re-election to the U.S. Senate and for the presidency in 2016. Kentucky Senate Majority Leader Damon Thayer confirmed he is working on a bill to clarify an ambiguous state law, which Paul believes could be unconstitutional if it prevents him from running for both offices. If successful, Paul could potentially win the Republican nomination for president while also retaining his Senate seat. However, this scenario faces opposition from the Democratic-controlled Kentucky House of Representatives. The situation has become more complex due to Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell's potential challenges in re-election and Paul's efforts to broaden the GOP base by supporting a bill restoring felons' voting rights.

A high school student in Lebanon, Tennessee, named Emily Gipson created an anti-bullying YouTube video titled "Welcome to Lebanon High School" after a classmate's suicide. The video, which garnered over 600,000 views, criticized both students and administrators for their handling of bullying and suicide prevention efforts at the school. Despite containing no profanity or direct calls for action, Gipson was given a two-day in-school suspension by her principal, who cited permission issues rather than the video's content.

Gipson's grandfather defended her actions, praising her for speaking out against what he sees as a significant issue in schools today. In response to the controversy and to encourage other students to speak up, Gipson posted another video titled "Have I Made a Difference Yet?" The incident has sparked debate about free speech, school policies, and the impact of student activism on social issues.

This ProPublica and NPR investigation highlights significant disparities in workers' compensation (WC) benefits across U.S. states, using the cases of Jeremy Lewis from Alabama and Josh Potter from Georgia. Both men lost a portion of their left arm at industrial plants but received vastly different outcomes due to state-specific WC laws.

Key points:
- Alabama has among the lowest WC benefits for amputations, while Georgia offers more generous compensation.
- The loss of an arm in Alabama is valued at $45,000, whereas in Georgia it could exceed $740,000 over a lifetime.
- These differences are due to state-level determinations with no federal minimums.
- Workers' comp benefits for body parts vary widely across states.
- Recent decades have seen a rollback of workers' comp protections nationwide, driven by employer and insurer demands to lower costs.

The document highlights issues at Wells Fargo, particularly through the experiences of Siham El-Dahan and Frank Ahn. El-Dahan, a former business banker, accused her managers of favoritism, denying employees required breaks, and threatening them to meet sales quotas. She claims she was fired in retaliation for complaining about these practices. Ahn, who runs a convenience store, reported that Wells Fargo opened multiple unnecessary accounts for him, leading to unauthorized charges and fees. He found it difficult to cancel the unwanted accounts due to his business's reliance on the bank's payment systems. Both El-Dahan and Ahn faced challenges in dealing with Wells Fargo's practices, with the bank declining to comment on their claims.

A marine engineer from Jamshedpur, India, named Saddam Hussain (now legally changed to Sajid), faces significant employment challenges due to his name. He graduated second in his class from Noorul Islam University in Tamil Nadu but has been unable to find a job with multinational shipping companies because of the negative connotations associated with his namesake, former Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein. Employers cite potential operational risks and complications when crossing borders as reasons for rejecting him.

Saddam attempted to change his name legally after realizing its impact on his career prospects. However, he faces bureaucratic hurdles in updating his educational certificates and other official documents. Despite these efforts, he continues to struggle with job applications and is currently awaiting a court hearing to expedite the process of changing his secondary school certificates.

The article highlights how Saddam Hussein's legacy still impacts individuals globally, even years after his execution, affecting their professional lives despite minor differences in spelling or name variations.

Emmis Digital conducted a unique "Intern Games" social media contest to select interns from over 25 applicants. The competition involved three finalists who had to drive social media engagement and attract followers for Emmis' platforms using hashtags like #TeamJake, #TeamKelsey, and #TeamKatie. In the end, both Kelsey Halverson and Jake Bouvy were chosen as winners, each excelling in different areas. This unconventional hiring method highlights the importance of digital skills and social media presence in today's job market. Employers are increasingly using social media to engage with potential employees before formal applications are submitted, emphasizing real-world experience over traditional resumes.

The search for missing Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 continues with no definitive findings after three days. Key points include:

- Two passengers used stolen passports to board the flight; FBI is checking their fingerprints.
- The search area has expanded, now covering hundreds of miles.
- Authorities are considering all possibilities, including terrorism and hijacking.
- Malaysian officials called for Malaysia to speed up its investigation efforts.
- Chinese relatives express frustration with limited information from the airline.
- Interpol confirmed stolen passports were on file but not checked against databases before departure.

The mystery remains unsolved as search teams continue their efforts in the South China Sea.

Chicago experienced its first January-February period without snow on the ground since records began in 1871, due to small amounts of snow melting before morning measurements. This record was overshadowed by severe storms and tornadoes, including one that killed a person in Ottowa. Meteorologists attribute this weather pattern to climate change but note natural variances can occur. The warm spell has had both positive and negative impacts, such as lower heating bills and concerns about early tree budding leading to frost damage. March brought significant snowfall, ending the record streak. Overall, experts warn that unusual weather events may become more frequent due to ongoing climate change.

Queen Elizabeth II highlighted family and friendship in her annual Christmas message, recorded before Prince Philip's hospitalization for a heart procedure. The royal family attended a Christmas service at St. Mary’s church on the Sandringham Estate, with Prince Philip absent due to his hospital stay. The Queen emphasized the importance of family as exemplified by her grandchildren's recent marriages and noted that family can provide strength during hardships. She also highlighted how friendships often form in challenging times. The royal gathering included Prince William, Kate (Duchess of Cambridge), Charles, Camilla, Harry, and other members of the family. After the service, children presented flowers to the Queen, who then handed them to her granddaughters. The annual Christmas message marks a rare opportunity for the Queen to express personal views without government consultation.

Thieves have stolen approximately 300 bottles of fine wine, valued at €250,000 (£230,500), from a cellar in central Paris. The theft occurred after the criminals broke into the catacombs and drilled through the wall of a property near the Luxembourg gardens, which houses the French Senate. The thieves then navigated the complex underground network to reach their target.

The Paris Catacombs, an extensive maze of tunnels containing about six million human remains, have been used for illegal activities such as parties and film screenings by groups known as 'Cataphiles.' Despite restrictions, these tunnels are occasionally accessed illegally. Police speculate that the thieves likely made multiple visits before executing the heist with precision.

The investigation is being handled by the 3rd District of the Parisian Criminal Investigation Department, but they have not yet commented on the case. The incident highlights both the historical significance and potential dangers associated with exploring the underground network beneath Paris.

Lambach (45), were arrested in Pittsfield, Massachusetts, on charges related to a citywide prostitution ring involving multiple women, some as young as 15. The investigation began after police received complaints of increased prostitution activity in the spring of 2017, mainly centered around certain streets.

Lambach allegedly recruited women with drug addictions, photographed them, and advertised their services online. He would arrange meetings, collect money, and sometimes provide drugs in lieu of cash. Some of the women were former foster children. Van Wert allowed some prostitution activities to take place in his apartment for drugs and cash. Lambach also transported the women and crossed state lines on at least one occasion.

The investigation involved multiple police units and led to arrests on November 14, with both men pleading not guilty. Additional charges may be forthcoming as the investigation continues.

Alexandria Duval, 38, is fighting extradition from New York to Hawaii where she faces a second-degree murder charge for allegedly driving her twin sister Anastasia off a cliff during a fight over the steering wheel. The incident occurred on May 29, 2016, in Maui, Hawaii. Duval was arrested in Albany, NY, after being tracked down by authorities. Her attorney argues that there is insufficient evidence to force extradition and that her client intends to return to New York for her sister's funeral. Bunce is a 21-year-old member of the U.S. Army's 105th Engineer Battalion and her husband believes her military training helped her stay calm during the confrontation. Theresa May survived a confidence vote from her Conservative Party but remains under pressure to resign due to opposition within her own ranks over Brexit. The vote, in which 200 MPs supported May and 117 voted against, highlights the party's deep divisions on the issue. May faces significant challenges as she tries to secure approval for her Brexit deal, with many critics arguing it does not fully honor the results of the 2016 referendum.

May canceled a parliamentary vote on her deal after it became clear she would lose badly and was subsequently challenged by Conservative MPs who believe her agreement is too closely tied to the EU. Despite support from cabinet ministers like Jeremy Hunt and Philip Hammond, May faces opposition from key figures such as Jacob Rees-Mogg. The Mo Ibrahim prize for African leadership has not awarded a winner in 2012, as no candidate met all the criteria. The $5 million prize is intended for democratically elected leaders who have raised living standards and voluntarily left office. Previous winners include Cape Verde's President Pedro Verona Pires (2011), Botswana's Festus Mogae (2007), and Mozambique's Joaquim Chissano (2006). Sofya Tsygankova, the estranged wife of acclaimed concert pianist Vadym Kholodenko, has been ruled mentally incompetent to stand trial for allegedly smothering their two young daughters with pillows. She is committed to a state mental health facility for 120 days of treatment in hopes that she will regain sufficient rational understanding to face justice. Tsygankova, 32, faces charges of capital murder and has pleaded not guilty. Vadym Kholodenko, who won the Van Cliburn International Piano Competition in 2013, resumed his musical career after the incident. Police found Tsygankova covered in blood with cuts on her wrists and the two children dead upon his arrival to pick up the girls for preschool. She had visited a mental health facility the day before the deaths and was found with an empty prescription bottle of quetiapine, an antipsychotic drug.

On June 2nd, as students lined up to sign each other's yearbooks during their final days of school, they also formed a long line to have Mr. Steve sign theirs. The enthusiasm was so great that a chair had to be brought out for him, and the queue extended around the playground. This spontaneous show of affection touched both Mr. Steve and the school administration, who noted his popularity with the students.
